# Rocker panel protection and repair

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Apply Herculiner coating material and pinstriping tape to protect rocker panels. [t769]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Start in a clean, dry area with good ventilation.
2. Lay down a drop cloth and arrange all materials within reach.
3. Tape off the target areas by aligning tape just below the centerline of door moldings.
4. [Partial] Secure the front inner fenderliners by unscrewing them and propping them away from the body.
5. Hook out the foam rubber door strip on the front edge of the rear doors using its white clips.
6. Tape around or over any remaining foam door trim at the bottom of the doors.
7. [Partial] Put on gloves to protect hands during application.
8. Wash the surface with soap and water to remove oils from the paint.
9. Sand the area thoroughly with a Scotch-Brite pad until the clearcoat is scuffed but not removed.
10. Wipe down the sanded sections with acetone, taking care not to let it sit too long.
11. Stir the Herculiner can gently for several minutes to suspend rubber particles without shaking it.
12. Pour the stirred mixture into a paint tray and apply a light first coat using a roller.
13. Fill in tight corners and edges missed by the roller with a small brush.
14. Wait 1-2 hours for the first coat to dry until it no longer sticks to your finger.
15. [Partial] Remove the painting tools from their protective bags while waiting.
16. Apply a second, thicker coat of Herculiner over the dried base layer.
17. [Partial] Immediately begin peeling back the blue painter's tape at a 180-degree angle away from the wet paint.
18. Place the used tape into an empty bucket to catch drips as you finish removing it all.
19. Apply pinstriping along the top edge of the Herculiner, following its contour closely.
20. Clean up any remaining tools and trash that have accumulated black spots on them.

_Procedure reported by [t769]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-for-2005-11-herculined-rocker-panels.387/>_

## Tools

- Paint roller [t769]
- Small paintbrush [t769]
- Paint tray [t769]
- Painters tape (blue variety recommended) [t769]
- Scotch brite pad or abrasive pad [t769]
- Acetone [t769]
- Rags [t769]
- Gloves (leather work gloves suggested) [t769]
- [Partial] Tarps [t769]

## Parts

- Herculiner coating material: A gallon can is recommended; a quart may be insufficient. [t769]
- Pinstriping tape, black 2-stripe: Optional for cleaning up edges and creating a factory look. [t769]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use blue painters tape as it works well; metal wire tape is an alternative. [t769]
- Stir the can rather than shaking it to keep rubber particles suspended. [t769]
- Apply pinstriping along the top edge of the coating, about 1/4 inch above for a factory look. [t769]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Applying too thickly in one go which causes pulling back up as it dries. [t769]
- [Partial] Waiting too long to remove tape after the second coat, leaving black spots on edges. [t769]
- [Partial] Getting product on skin and not wiping immediately with acetone. [t769]
